Alicia H.: quick sync — we need a small UX sketch for the automatic fallback policy in Rollouts. Product wants defaults + audit. What are the must-haves?
Vivek: must-haves = clear degrade modes, visible trigger rules, and an explanation for "why" when fallback fires. also need API parity so infra can use same config.
Olga: agree. UX should let users pick between fail-closed, fail-open, and degraded-mode (cheaper/quantized model). also per-route overrides.
Kevin (product): product ask: sensible default that is safe for customer apps. proposing: default -> "degrade to compatible variant" (same model family, lower cost) rather than routing to a different family. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
Randall: security note — audit logs for fallbacks must be PII-safe. If we capture request payloads in the audit, need redaction pipeline or sampled capture. Also retention TTL options.
Alicia H.: UX: in console rollout detail page show a timeline band with markers for fallback events. click marker -> small panel: trigger (latency/error), chosen fallback, request-id samples, and a link to redaction view.
Vivek: API sketch so backend teams can start: ```yaml
fallback_policy:
  mode: degrade  # options: fail-closed | fail-open | degrade | route-to-backup
  fallback_model: rdx-small-1q  # optional, or auto-choose compatible variant
  triggers:
    latency_ms: 1500
    error_rate: 0.05
    spike_window_s: 30
  audit: true  # capture metadata+sampled payloads
  audit_retention_days: 30
  notify: ["oncall","owner@example.com"]
```
Olga: small UX debate: should we surface "auto-select compatible variant" as a toggle, or let users pick a specific fallback model? If auto-select, add tooltip: "selects same-arch quantized/cheaper build".
Kevin (product): prefer auto-select as default but leave explicit override. Keeps onboarding simple. Docs must show fallback ranking rules.
Randall: plus RBAC controls: who can read audit exports, who can toggle fallbacks. Also need a compliance flag for enterprise customers to disable sampled payload capture.
Vivek: implementation note: runtime needs fast decision path. Suggest policy compiled down to a match tree and pre-wired fallbacks per model shard. We'll add a policy version and eval hash to aid audits.
Alicia H.: UX wire: on rollout create flow add "Fallback behavior" step with small presets: Safe (fail-closed + notify), Balanced (degrade + auto-select), Open (fail-open). Each shows consequences and example latency/cost tradeoffs.
Olga: minimal console copy for the band: "Fallbacks: 3 triggered (last 6h). Click to inspect." Clicking shows the trigger counts and per-trigger breakdown (timeouts, errors, latency).
Kevin (product): metrics we need surfaced: #fallbacks, average latency pre/post fallback, %requests affected, cost delta. Also ability to export events as CSV for audits.
Randall: add an "explain why" payload — include the decision metadata: policy_version, matched_trigger, model_chosen, runtime_metrics. Make sure any included inputs are redacted unless customer opts in.
deploy-bot: deploy event: rollout/rdx-v2 -> canary started at 2024-06-17T15:12:03Z :rocket:
Vivek: final ask: let's add a system-level default policy that is conservative (fail-closed) and a per-organization template that product can set. Then user can opt-in to more permissive templates.
Alicia H.: action items: 1) Vivek: finalize API schema + minimal example by EOD. 2) Olga: wireframe for create-rollout fallback step + timeline panel by midweek. 3) Kevin: write copy for presets + docs. 4) Randall: compliance requirements & redaction options. I'll collect and post a single spec next week. :+1:
Kevin (product): thanks — will sync with legal on retention.
Olga: one UX edge case — what about multi-model chains? fallback should be per-route in a chain; we need a clear way to express that in the UI (dropdown per step). Noted.
Alicia H.: great, please add any small mocks here when ready.
